maya: Quick heads-up — offline A/B replay shows a surprising p99 spike when the token-governor is enabled alongside the new kernel selector. Posting summary and logs.

sam: Numbers?

maya: Summary from the offline run (full logs attached to the replay artifact):
```
Control (heuristic_v2):
 p50 45ms  p95 120ms  p99 210ms  tokens/s 18.2  cost/token $0.00080
Experiment (heuristic_v3 + token_governor):
 p50 48ms  p95 125ms  p99 420ms  tokens/s 17.1  cost/token $0.00077
Note: throughput slightly down, but p99 doubled.
```

cheng: Is this from trace-driven sim or live traffic replay? Can you share trace ids and the exact sim command?

maya: Replay was trace-driven (sample: may-release-ops-2026), offline-sim v0.9.3, AB mode. Config excerpt: token_governor.target_tokens=256, burst_shaper=0.8, kernel_selector=heuristic_v3, kv_prefetch.threshold=0.4. Command I used: 
```
./sim/run_replay --traces=/traces/may-release-ops-2026.tgz --config=heuristic_v3.toml --mode=ab --seed=42 --out=/replays/2119876543
```

irene: Did we also change any KV warmup/prefetch policy? Increased misses there can blow up tail latency.

maya: We did tweak kv_prefetch.threshold from 0.6 -> 0.4 in heuristic_v3 to reduce cold misses, but maybe the governor changes scheduling and causes more kernel preemptions/fragmentation.

perf-bot: perf-ci: offline-replay completed for job 2119876543-abrun — p99 regression flagged. Artifacts uploaded to: /replays/2119876543 (metrics.csv, kernel-switch.log, kv-stats.json)

cheng: Quick sanity check: can you repro with prefetch disabled? That'll isolate KV effect vs kernel-governor interaction. Run single-epoch replay: 
```
./sim/run_replay --traces=/traces/may-release-ops-2026.tgz --config=kernel_v3.toml --overrides=prefetch.enabled=false --ab=control --seed=42
```

sam: Ran a small subset locally. p99 didn't move for control, but experiment shows a big uptick in kernel-switch counts. Looks like kernel churn at longer seq lengths (requests crossing selector thresholds) — multiple switches per request.

maya: Kernel-switch log snippet: `KERNEL_SWITCH req=0x7f3b2 seq_prev=512 seq_new=1024 at token=512` — happening repeatedly for many requests. If we switch kernels mid-request, we see stalls while caches/warmups settle.

irene: Proposal: for canary, 1) increase kernel hysteresis to avoid switching until delta >= 30% sequence delta, 2) bump token_governor.target_tokens to 320 to reduce preemption, 3) gate KV prefetch to avoid prefetch during a kernel change window. Also capture kv.hit_rate and ttfb per-request.

maya: I'll kick off a canary replay with those params and collect kv hit-rate, kernel-switch counts, and p99 breakdown by model length. Tagging @cheng to watch the run. Command I'll use: 
```
./sim/run_replay --traces=/traces/may-release-ops-2026.tgz --config=canary_hysteresis320.toml --mode=ab --out=/replays/2119876543-canary --seed=1337
```

cheng: Got it. Watchlist: p99 change, kernel-switches per-request, kv_miss_rate, and tokens/sec. Rollback criteria: if p99 > +50% relative to control or kv_miss_rate increases by >5pp.

maya: Running now. I'll post summaries when the artifacts finish uploading. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy: triggered replay-canary job 2119876599 (watch at /replays/2119876543-canary)

cheng: Thanks — will validate results and decide whether to merge heuristic_v3 adjustments or iterate further.

sam: If canary looks good, let's also add an A/B in the live offline-sampler with a narrow user cohort before any prod rollout.

maya: Agreed. TY everyone.
